uncited: This article describes the standard software architecture for implementing direct volume ray casting on modern GPUs using OpenGL and GLSL.
It details the pipeline for generating spherical harmonic (SH) coefficient volumes and performing ray marching via fragment shaders.
The core challenge addressed is the integration of three functions (material function $M$, incoming light $L_{mi}$, and outgoing light $L_{mi}^0$) which is complex for direct SH integration.
*   **Input:** Volume data, material properties, lighting conditions (represented as SH coefficients), and pre-generated random sample directions.
*   Normalized Cartesian vectors for Monte Carlo sampling.
*   **Random Number Generation:** The GLSL specification describes functionality for generating random numbers, but this feature was not implemented in the referenced environment.
